## Body

# reviewer verdict, PR #343 at 59db7f90dccfc590de2e2a79d2dd16df8996161e: BLOCK (F1 only)

One round (C34). The block is narrow: F1 is one committed script and one recipe in PROC-fleet-0001. The runner, the
shim route, the check stage, the Rust pins and the privacy sweep pass. Fix F1 and F2; the notes are optional.

## Must fix

**F1 (security, contradicts req-13, which is marked shipped).**
`docs/project/procedures/fleet/PROC-fleet-0001-change-seat-effort/relaunch.sh` builds
`tmux respawn-pane ... "env $envs $launcher $flags --effort $effort --resume=$session"`.
- (a) `$envs` is every `PIJ_*`/`COPILOT_*` **value** read from `ps -E`. They become argv of the tmux client, the pane's
  `sh -c` and `env`: readable by every local user through `ps` and logged by Defender's EDR. A BYOK
  `COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY` or a `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` in a seat's env would leak. req-13 says "no step ... puts one in
  an argument list", and the script's own header says "never their values". Drafts run (req-21), so this is live today,
  behind only the self-attested s0001 decision.
- (b) The string is run by `sh`, and the values in it are unquoted: `PROC_IN_EFFORT` (an `--arg`), the env values and
  the `ps` flags are split into words or executed (`--arg effort='high; <cmd>'`). Values with spaces break the relaunch.
- (c) The `effort-is` recipe (the done check for s0002 and s0003) puts `$PROC_IN_EFFORT` into a regex:
  `--arg effort='.*'` makes the done check pass.
- Fix: validate the effort against the values Copilot accepts (an allowlist, in the script and in `effort-is`). Carry an
  allowlist of known non-secret names, or skip any name matching `KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASS`, and pass the env through a
  0600 file the pane command sources and then deletes, never on a command line. Quote every word you interpolate
  (`'` becomes `'\''`).

**F2 (correctness, low).** `--key` is never validated. Reproduced with `saveRecord`/`readProgress` in a scratch root:
`--key __proto__`, `constructor` or `toString` persists nothing (the stored run is `{}`), and with `__proto__` it sets
`Object.prototype.s0001` in the process, so `recordOf` then reads that step as done for any key in that process. The
key is also printed unquoted into the suggested `next:` commands. Fix: refuse a key outside `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@-]*$`,
and read records with `Object.hasOwn`.

## Notes (optional)

- N1, a test gap. Mutant M2 survives: changing the before-run done check from `=== 0` to `!== 1` still passes 31/31.
  The code is right, but nothing pins that a done check exiting 2, 127 or on a signal is not done. Add one test with
  `exit 2`.
- N2. Progress is read, modified and written back with no lock. Two runs with different keys at once (the case the
  comment names) can lose a record, because the last rename wins. Use a lock file opened with O_EXCL, or a file per
  key.
- N3. Preconditions and done checks have no timeout, so a hanging check hangs the runner. It only runs on demand, so
  this is a note.
- N4. In the justfile, `proc` and `procedures-check` sit between pr-freeze's ten-line comment and its recipe, so that
  comment now heads `proc`. Move them.
- N5. The workstream's s08 is still `planned`, although the report says it was delivered at 59db7f90 (a state for pm-001
  to set).
- N6. A procedure's inputs, secret ones included, reach another procedure's `requires` done check through the env
  (`envFor(other, …)`). That's env only, so req-13 holds, but it is wider than needed.

## Checked and passing

- **Injection.** `spawnSync` runs with no shell. The recipe word must be a recipe a justfile defines
  (`[A-Za-z_]…`, read in-process), with `--justfile` and `--working-directory` fixed. `--arg` values and the key reach
  recipes only through the env (`PROC_IN_*`, `PROC_KEY`). Every other procedure recipe quotes `"$PROC_IN_*"`. `new`
  checks the area and slug against regexes before `pij claim`. `status` passes its values as ddocs argv and through
  `JSON.stringify`.
- **Secrets.** A secret `--arg` is refused (mutant M3 detected). Progress records only at, by, how and note, never
  inputs. Refusals print an input's description, never its value. The runner emits no spine events.
- **Paths.** `requires` resolves only to loaded procedures. The configured home refuses absolute paths and `..`.
  `follow` is only printed. Progress is at `<common git dir>/pij-procedures/progress.json`, mode 0644, written to a
  temp file and renamed, and holds no secrets.
- **Shim.** `pij proc` only calls `runner.main(rest, realIo())`. `invokedDirectly()` is false under `require`, so
  nothing runs twice. I ran it from a scratch copy: `proc list` worked, and `PROC-fleet-0001 s0002` was refused before
  s0001.
- **Correctness.** Order inside a procedure (M5 detected), order across procedures through the live done check (M4),
  preconditions refusing (M6) and the after-run done check being required (M1) are all held by tests. A second run
  with a passing done check and an existing record writes nothing. A missing recipe or a spawn error is never counted
  as done (127 or 1). Approval with `status` needs `--approved-by` and `--why`; who approved is stated, not enforced
  (q-05, as designed).
- **Rust.** The `shasum -a 256` of coder v5 (b40f6e8d…) and reviewer v4 (b296f487…) equal the pinned values, and
  `include_bytes!` reads those files. `SHIM_LOCAL_VERBS` skips only the exact `words[1]` values `fleet-map` and `proc`,
  still checks their placeholders, and every other verb is checked as before. rust-test is green at the exact head. I
  did not build locally (31 GB free, near the floor).
- **Cost.** No loop, poll, timer or hook in the runner. `just procedures-check` took 0.46 s wall: one `git ls-files` and
  one `just --summary` per procedure justfile, so it grows linearly with procedures. `report` runs one `git grep` per
  path only one procedure uses, on demand. Recipes go through `nice19.sh`. The relaunch's wait (at most 30 × `pij list`
  at 2 s) is bounded, once per run.
- **`.omp/extensions/pij/cli.ts`.** One help line, no logic.
- **Privacy.** No `/Users`, `/var/folders` or home paths, account names or emails in the added lines. osk-central
  appears by name and through seat names only, and the survey leaves out its infrastructure, vendors and findings on
  purpose.
